questions.q: Why are anonymous MySQL accounts a documented security weakness rather than a hypothetical one?
options: Some default installs historically created an account with an empty username that could connect, and in some cases even create a database
They only exist in theoretical attack scenarios and have never been exploited
They are a MyISAM-only issue and don't affect InnoDB
Anonymous accounts are automatically disabled by default in every MySQL version
questions.explain: This is a real, well-known default weakness that mysql_secure_installation explicitly addresses by removing them.

questions.q: What does disallowing remote root login accomplish?
options: It restricts root to connecting only from localhost, closing off network-based attacks on the highest-value account
It deletes the root account entirely
It prevents root from running any SQL statements
It only affects MyISAM tables
questions.explain: Even with a strong password, an account reachable over the network is a bigger attack surface than one reachable only locally.

questions.q: What does the bind-address setting in my.cnf control?
options: Which network interface(s) the MySQL server listens on
The default storage engine for new tables
The root account's password
Which databases mysql_secure_installation removes
questions.explain: bind-address should be set to a specific interface rather than left open to all networks unnecessarily.

questions.q: Which query lists every account (user and host pair) that exists on a MySQL server?
options: SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user;
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'accounts';
SHOW ENGINES;
SELECT * FROM information_schema.tables;
questions.explain: mysql.user is the system table listing every account, used for auditing unused or unexplained accounts.

questions.q: What is 'privilege creep', per this lesson?
options: Access that accumulates over time on an account and outlives its original justification
A performance issue caused by too many GRANT statements
A MySQL bug that silently changes privilege levels
The automatic expansion of a role's privileges over time
questions.explain: Privilege creep is why a periodic audit pass, cross-checking SHOW GRANTS against actual need, matters.
